newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti net debt 2.92 trln lire end-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti net debt 2.92 trln lire end-Nov.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said its net financial debt stood at 2.916 trillion lire at the end of November 1996.

Olivetti said in a statement released after the Milan stock market ended its final trading session of 1996 that group operations had generated cash amounting to 112 billion lire, reducing net financial debt from 3.028 trillion at the end of October.

"This result does not take into account the financial effect of extraordinary items such as the sale of the 8.26 percent holding in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari which will be recorded in the group's statement of financial condition for December 1996," the Olivetti statement said, adding the fall in debt was mostly due to a reduction in working capital.
Net book indebtedness at end-November amounted to 2.419 trillion, a decrease of 132 billion lire from October.

The November figure included the sale of 430 billion lire of trade receivables, with 253 billion of that from a securitisation programme and 177 billion from factoring operations, and the deferral of 67 billion in payments to suppliers.
Shortly before the news was announced, Olivetti shares ended 1.56 percent higher at 532.4 lire in a weak Milan stock market.
